plan: My value is $3. Since the goal is to maximize profit in the long run, and this is the only round, I need to maximize profit in this round. The game explicitly states "it is always safe to bid above your value---winning can never cost you more than the item is worth to you." This implies I should bid high enough to guarantee a win if I want to, as my profit is determined by my value minus the second-highest bid. To maximize my chances of winning and thus profit, I will bid the maximum possible value, which is $49.

My value is $24. Since I win and pay the second-highest bid, bidding above my value is safe. To maximize profit, I want to win when my value is high, and pay as little as possible. Given the single round, and no prior history, a simple strategy is to bid slightly above my value to ensure I win if the other bids are below my value. I will bid $24.1.

Given my value of $11, I want to win if the second-highest bid is below $11. The optimal strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value. This ensures I win when it's profitable and never pay more than my value. I will bid $11.00.
